doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Joining the Harlem Blues & Jazz Band
summary: Blue came into the band as the baby after Doc Vollmer heard him at a union hall jam session, joining veterans like Art Baron and Zeke Mullins.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Let me wrap up with asking you what it’s been like to — you had a long tenure with the Harlem Blues & Jazz Band, and shared the stage with some older gentlemen. I wonder what that’s been like?

It’s been wonderful you know. I came into that band as the baby. Doc [Vollmer] came to one of the sessions, the jam sessions at the union hall and that’s where he heard me, and he liked what I was doing and he spoke with me, and he pulled me in as a back-up or a sub for Fred.

Because Fred was, his health was starting to be more challenged, you know, and that was — and Joey Morant was there and Art Baron on trombone. Now Art had played with, in the Ellington band when Duke was still leading it, and he’s got a lot of experience and stories and a great musician. Jackie [Williams], and Jackie on drums. The stories these cats had, and you learn man, it’s all about learning. Zeke Mullins — Zeke was Hamp’s piano player for what 20-some years? You know and Zeke, old Zeke man, they were really great guys. And at the time Ruth Brisbane was singing and I loved her voice, I loved her voice man and she —
Yeah, she had that church Gospel combination with pig foot and a bottle of beer or something like that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
